slides.1.title: Rosé
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Appearance
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Pale orange-pink to salmon; very pale colour is the Provençal signature
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Nose
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Red berries, citrus, white peach, herbs and Mediterranean scrub
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Palate
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Dry, crisp, medium body, fine acidity; better wines have more structure
slides.1.content: Pale and dry is the style.
slides.2.title: White and red
slides.2.highlights.0.title: White
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Vermentino, Clairette and Ugni Blanc: citrus, herbs, minerality
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Red
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Cinsault: from soft to structured
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Wind and sun
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Mistral and sunshine concentrate the fruit and keep disease low
slides.2.content: Wind and sun shape clean flavours.
slides.3.title: Food pairing
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Seafood
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Bouillabaisse, grilled fish and oysters suit white or pale rosé
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Provençal cuisine
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Ratatouille, tapenade and aïoli suit rosé
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Meat
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Braised lamb and herb-roasted meats suit Bandol and Sartène reds
slides.3.content: Mediterranean food and wine belong together.
